newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian govt, unions agree local job deals - papers.
newsitem.headline: Italian govt, unions agree local job deals - papers.

text.p: The Italian government, employers and trades unions have agreed a deal on flexible wages and working hours in key areas to help create jobs in the impoverished south, newspapers reported on Saturday.
The Corriere della Sera newspaper said some salaries could be as much as 25 to 30 percent lower as a result of the agreement which was due to be introduced in 10 pilot areas before 52 other zones.
The daily Unita newspaper said under the accord, industry and banks would make credit more available in exchange for unions agreeing flexibility on wages for a limited period of time.
It said those involved would be young people looking for a job, long-term unemployed and redundant workers.
L'Unita said the government would draft a law, possibly in the 1997 budget, to overcome legislative obstacles.
The accord was welcomed by business leaders at an international forum in northern Italy.
Marco Tronchetti Provera, chairman of Italian tyre and cable maker Pirelli, called the agreement was a good first step which should be followed by others.
Tronchetti Provera said it was "an intervention which should be accompanied by a system of fiscal actions, which guarantee the incentive to invest in the area."
